chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no breast-feeding (creating kinship) after weaning.' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! And what is the weaning?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The two years which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, speaks of.'
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of weaning in Shia jurisprudence regarding breast-feeding kinship?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the temporal limit for breast-feeding to establish mahramiyah, defining weaning as the completion of two years (al-hawlayn) based on Quranic precedent. It reflects the Shia scholarly consensus that nursing after this age does not create marital prohibitions, distinguishing between the biological act and its legal consequences. The reference to 'al-hawlayn' anchors the ruling in the Quranic narrative of Prophet Muhammad's (PBUH) weaning, emphasizing the continuity between divine text and Imami jurisprudence.
